testDefinitions.displayName: Identification of Aluminium Magnesium Silicate (reaction of silicates)
testDefinitions.notes: In platinum crucible mix 1.0 g with 5.0 g anhydrous lithium metaborate; ignite at 1000-1200 °C for 15 min; crush residue; mix 0.25 g residue with 10 mg NaF and a few drops H2SO4; warm gently under plastic plate with drop of water: white ring rapidly formed (BP 2024 Appendix VI Silicates; source: Veegum__STM Veegum.txt:32).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification of Aluminium Magnesium Silicate (aluminium reaction with phenolphthalein and NaF)
testDefinitions.notes: Dissolve 1.0 g residue from test A in 5 mL dilute HCl and 10 mL water; filter; add ammonium chloride buffer pH 10.0 (white gelatinous precipitate); dissolve precipitate in dilute HCl, add dropwise dilute NaOH (white gelatinous precipitate); filter, add phenolphthalein to residue (turns pink); wash until pink discharges, sprinkle NaF crystals: turns pink again (source: Veegum__STM Veegum.txt:32).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification of Aluminium Magnesium Silicate (magnesium reaction with phosphate)
testDefinitions.notes: To 2 mL supernatant from test B add 1 mL dilute ammonia R1 and 1 mL ammonium chloride solution; add 1 mL disodium hydrogen phosphate solution: white precipitate forms (source: Veegum__STM Veegum.txt:32).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification of Aluminium Magnesium Silicate (AAS, comply with assay)
testDefinitions.notes: Complies with limits of the assay for aluminium and magnesium (source: Veegum__STM Veegum.txt:32).

testDefinitions.displayName: Acid demand of Aluminium Magnesium Silicate
testDefinitions.notes: Weigh quantity equivalent to 5.00 g dried substance in 500 mL water. With constant mixing, add 3.0 mL portions of 0.1 M HCl at 5, 65, 125, 185, 245, 305, 365, 425, 485, 545, 605, 665, 725 s, and 1.0 mL at 785 s. Determine pH at 840 s: pH NMT 4.0 (source: Veegum__STM Veegum.txt:38).

testDefinitions.displayName: Assay of Aluminium Magnesium Silicate (Al/Mg ratio by AAS)
testDefinitions.notes: 0.200 g ignited with 1.0 g lithium metaborate at 1000-1200 °C for 15 min, dissolved in 50 g/L HNO3 to 200.0 mL (solution A). Al measured at 309 nm (N2O-acetylene) vs 10-40 µg/mL Al standards with NaCl. Mg measured at 285 nm (air-acetylene) vs 0.5-2.0 µg/mL Mg standards with LaCl3. Ratio of Al content to Mg content: 0.5 to 1.2. Result entered by analyst (ratio cannot be calculated by standard AAS/ICP workflows; CATALOG.md rule 6; source: Veegum__STM Veegum.txt:39).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification of Calcium Glycerophosphate (reaction with KHSO4 and piperidine)
testDefinitions.notes: Mix 1 g with 1 g KHSO4, heat strongly, direct vapour to filter paper impregnated with 10 g/L sodium nitroprusside: develops blue colour in contact with piperidine (BP 2024 Monograph; source: Calcium Glycerophosphate__Calcium Glycerophosphate-SM.txt:30).

testDefinitions.displayName: Citric acid test for Calcium Glycerophosphate
testDefinitions.notes: Shake 5.0 g with 20 mL CO2-free water, filter; add 0.15 mL H2SO4, filter; add 5 mL mercuric sulfate solution, heat to boiling; add 0.5 mL 3.2 g/L KMnO4, heat to boiling: no precipitate formed (BP 2024 Monograph; source: Calcium Glycerophosphate__Calcium Glycerophosphate-SM.txt:33).

testDefinitions.displayName: Glycerol and ethanol-soluble substances in Calcium Glycerophosphate
testDefinitions.notes: Shake 1.000 g with 25 mL ethanol (96%) for 1 min, filter, evaporate filtrate on water bath, dry residue at 70 °C for 1 h, weigh beaker with residue: residue NMT 5 mg / 0.5% (BP 2024 Monograph; source: Calcium Glycerophosphate__Calcium Glycerophosphate-SM.txt:34).

Dilute 2.5 mL solution S to 100 mL with water; add 4 mL sulfomolybdic reagent R3, shake, add 0.1 mL stannous chloride R1; standard 2 mL phosphate standard (5 ppm PO4) + 98 mL water. After 10 min, compare colours (NMT 400 ppm). (BP Appendix VII Limit Tests Phosphates; source: Calcium Glycerophosphate__Calcium Glycerophosphate-SM.txt:36).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification of Copper Sulfate Pentahydrate (reactions of copper)
testDefinitions.notes: 0.1 g in 1 mL water + 1 mL dilute ammonia: blue precipitate dissolving to deep blue; add 1 mL dilute acetic acid and 1 mL potassium ferrocyanide: reddish-brown precipitate (BP Appendix VI Copper; source: Cooper Sulfate Pentahydrate__Copper Sulphate pentahydrate-SM.txt:30).

testDefinitions.displayName: Nickel (limit test by AAS for Copper Sulfate Pentahydrate)
testDefinitions.notes: 0.5 g in 10 mL water + 2.5 mL lead-free HNO3 to 25.0 mL; measured by flame AAS at 232.0 nm (air-acetylene) vs nickel standard 0.5 ppm Ni (NMT 1 ppm). (BP Appendix II D; source: Cooper Sulfate Pentahydrate__Copper Sulphate pentahydrate-SM.txt:33).

testDefinitions.displayName: Cobalt (limit test by AAS for Copper Sulfate Pentahydrate)
testDefinitions.notes: 0.5 g in 10 mL water + 2.5 mL lead-free HNO3 to 25.0 mL; measured by flame AAS at 240.7 nm (air-acetylene) vs cobalt standard 0.5 ppm Co (NMT 1 ppm). (BP Appendix II D; source: Cooper Sulfate Pentahydrate__Copper Sulphate pentahydrate-SM.txt:34).

testDefinitions.displayName: Iron (limit test by AAS for Copper Sulfate Pentahydrate)
testDefinitions.notes: 0.5 g in 10 mL water + 2.5 mL lead-free HNO3 to 25.0 mL; measured by flame AAS at 248.3 nm (air-acetylene) vs iron standard 20 ppm Fe (NMT 100 ppm). (BP Appendix II D; source: Cooper Sulfate Pentahydrate__Copper Sulphate pentahydrate-SM.txt:36).

testDefinitions.displayName: Assay of Copper Sulfate Pentahydrate (iodometric titration)
testDefinitions.titrationEquivalencyFactorDerivation: 24.97 mg CuSO4·5H2O per mL 0.1 M (0.1 N) sodium thiosulfate / 0.1 = 249.7 mg/mmol
testDefinitions.notes: 0.200 g dissolved in 50 mL water + 2 mL sulfuric acid + 3 g potassium iodide; titrate with 0.1 M (0.1 N) sodium thiosulfate VS, adding 1 mL starch solution near the end. 1 mL 0.1 M sodium thiosulfate = 24.97 mg CuSO4·5H2O. Limit: 99.0%-101.0% (BP Appendix VIII D; source: Cooper Sulfate Pentahydrate__Copper Sulphate pentahydrate-SM.txt:38).
